full_judgment: 4. In this respect the learned Advocate submits that admittedly the deceased was killed, but who murdered? The prosecution has hopelessly failed to prove, who murdered the deceased. Although the prosecution must prove the case beyond any reasonable doubt and nobody should be punished or convicted on mere conjecture and surmise as some body was murdered and the court must be confined within the materials on record and mainly on the evidence available before it. There is no place of moral conviction in dispensation of justice and presumption cannot take the place of proof.
